name: Ghostery Private Browser
businessModel: Free; Ghostery GmbH funds itself through its other products (extension subscriptions and related services), not the browser. Exact revenue link unverified.
statusNote: Sunset announced 2024-12-05; no security or feature updates since the final 2024.8.2 build (Dec 2024); GitHub repo archived 2025-02-17. Ghostery now recommends Firefox or Safari plus its extension.
pitch: Firefox-based browser with Ghostery blocking built in. Discontinued in Dec 2024.
summary: A Firefox fork (formerly Dawn) with Ghostery tracker and ad blocking built in. Ghostery retired it in December 2024 and tells users to keep Firefox or Safari and add the Ghostery extension instead.
bestFor: Nobody new: the browser no longer receives security updates
Existing users looking for the replacement path (Firefox + Ghostery extension)
Readers comparing how a Firefox-based privacy browser was packaged
notFor: Anyone who needs security fixes for a browser that is exposed to the open web
People who want a maintained browser with a roadmap
Users who need a mobile version (the mobile apps were retired too)

pros.title: Blocking built in
pros.detail: Ghostery positioned it as blocking ads and trackers out of the box, without installing an extension.

pros.title: Firefox base
pros.detail: Built on Firefox, so Firefox extensions and the Gecko engine were available.

pros.title: Open source
pros.detail: The full desktop source was public under MPL-2.0 and remains readable in the archived repository.

pros.title: Clear exit path
pros.detail: Ghostery explained the shutdown and named replacements for desktop, Android and iOS.

cons.title: Discontinued
cons.detail: Ghostery says the browser no longer gets security or feature updates and that continued use is at your own risk.

cons.title: Frozen engine
cons.detail: The Firefox base has not been updated since late 2024, so known browser vulnerabilities stay unpatched.

cons.title: No mobile option
cons.detail: Android and iOS users are pointed to Firefox and Safari with the Ghostery extension instead.

cons.title: Thin documentation
cons.detail: Telemetry, sync and DRM behaviour of the final builds are not documented in any source we could fetch.

faq.q: Is Ghostery Private Browser still supported?
faq.a: No. Ghostery announced the sunset on 2024-12-05 and the repository was archived on 2025-02-17; the browser gets no security or feature updates.
Ghostery recommends Firefox with the Ghostery Tracker & Ad Blocker extension on desktop and Android, and Safari with the extension on iOS and iPadOS.
Ghostery said Safari on iOS (since 2022) and Firefox on Android (since 2024) now support extensions, so a standalone browser was no longer necessary.

timeline.event: Desktop repository created on GitHub (as Dawn)
Ghostery blog introduces the Private Browser as a faster, Firefox-based browser
Sunset announced on 5 Dec; final release posted 10 Dec
GitHub repository archived and marked discontinued
